KKR.thesis_one_line: A top-3 alternative asset manager with an insurance arm, growing fees fast, priced by the market for far less growth than it is delivering.
kill_criteria: Fee Paying AUM growth decelerates below 5% YoY for two consecutive quarters
A confirmed, material adverse regulatory finding or settlement tied to the Global Atlantic third-party-administrator litigation disclosed in the FY2025 10-K
ANI per Adjusted Share declines YoY for two consecutive quarters
Consolidated Global Atlantic statutory capital/RBC ratio falls below regulatory comfort levels
LTM New Capital Raised falls more than 30% YoY (it was a record $133bn LTM at 2Q'26; the earlier '$4.68bn' figure was FRE per adjusted share)
key_adverse_facts: Q04 triage flagged the worst statistical-model rank in the batch (495/500) and negative 12-month momentum (-15%), tied to Global Atlantic insurance/private-credit risk
Global Atlantic was, per the FY2025 10-K, the subject of policyholder and agent class action litigation and regulatory matters stemming from service disruptions caused by a third-party administrator

Could not cleanly separate parent-only leverage from consolidated (insurance-inclusive) leverage this pass; the 2Q'26 release shows Asset Management and Strategic Holdings debt at par of $9.3bn against GAAP debt obligations of $49.7bn (verification DVH6)
GAAP net income swings quarter to quarter are large (1Q'26 $405.2m vs 2Q'26 $700.5m, +73% sequential) given no forward guidance is given by the company
ANI adds back ~$0.74bn of LTM equity-based compensation, so ANI-based valuation flatters cash earnings (verification DVH6)
data_conflicts: None identified versus v1 (no v1 row exists for KKR)
KKR.confidence_in_thesis: med (fee-earning franchise growth is well evidenced; Global Atlantic insurance-book risk and parent-vs-consolidated leverage were not fully disaggregated this pass)

LH.thesis_one_line: America's leading clinical-lab duopoly player, cheapest of its peers and with 2026-29 outlook reaffirmed after the CMS preliminary PAMA cuts of 21 Sep, but the price (5.6% implied 10-year FCF growth at a 9.5% cost of equity) now sits in line with a PAMA-adjusted 6.5-7.5% base.
kill_criteria: Full-year adjusted EPS guidance is cut (not just maintained) at any of the next two quarterly releases (next: 28 Oct 2026)
Enterprise revenue growth falls below 3% YoY for two consecutive quarters
Free cash flow conversion (FCF / adjusted net income) falls below 70% on a trailing-four-quarter basis (the single-quarter test is seasonal: Q1 2026 OCF was only $191.5m)
A material adverse ruling or settlement in the pending qui tam/DOJ matters disclosed in the FY2025 10-K
Net debt/EBITDA rises above 3.0x (net debt $5.72bn at 30 Jun 2026, ex leases; ratio not yet computed)
Final CMS 2027 CLFS rates (Nov 2026) keep the ~-16% average cuts with no Congressional delay by year-end, or the Feb 2027 FY27 guide implies adjusted EPS growth below 5%
key_adverse_facts: Company is a repeat subject of qui tam False Claims Act suits and received a DOJ subpoena (served June 27, 2022) requiring production of documents related to urine drug testing, with which it is cooperating, per the FY2025 10-K
Cash fell from $981.1m (2026-03-31) to $141.8m (2026-06-30) while long-term debt rose from $5,084.6m (2025-12-31) to $5,857.6m (2026-06-30); the specific cause was not independently sourced this pass
Operating cash flow was roughly flat YoY (1H'26 $637.0m vs 1H'25 $639.1m) despite GAAP EPS growth of 28.5% YoY in the quarter, worth monitoring for a widening working-capital or one-off gap

CMS preliminary 2027-2029 PAMA rates (press release 21 Sep 2026): Medicare paying ~16% above private payers, ~$1bn a year savings, cuts capped at 15% a year through 2029; final rates Nov 2026. Labcorp's 22 Sep 8-K reaffirmed the 2026-29 outlook (adjusted EPS CAGR 8.5-11.5%, FCF growth in line) but will quantify 2027 only in Feb 2027; Mizuho estimates ~$100m year-one hit (third party)

1H26 FCF $384m, -12% YoY (Q2 -42%) while adjusted EPS grew; 2H26 needs ~$916m (+19% vs 2H25) to meet the $1.3bn guide midpoint; net debt rose $664m in six months to $5.72bn on $452m of buybacks and $428m of acquisitions
At a rf-consistent 9.5% cost of equity (10-year Treasury 5.17% on 25 Sep after the 16 Sep Fed hike) the price implies ~5.6% 10-year FCF growth versus 3.4% at the dossier's 8.5%
data_conflicts: None identified versus v1 (no v1 row exists for LH)

Open item resolved: June cash fall explained by Q2 buybacks $353.8m and acquisitions $225.7m (XBRL). Red-team claims not supported: net debt up ~$1.2bn (actual +$664m); MLM Medical Labs (closed 8 Sep) as the cause of the June cash drop (post-dates 30 Jun). Dividend yield ~1.0%, not ~1.3%. Q3 earnings date confirmed 28 Oct 2026 (8-K), not 29 Oct
LH.confidence_in_thesis: medium - guidance reaffirmed after the CMS release and valuation is the cheapest in the peer set, but 1H FCF is down 12%, PAMA 2027 impact is unquantified until Feb 2027, and the reverse-DCF cushion has narrowed

NI.thesis_one_line: An Indiana/Ohio gas-and-electric utility funding a large, regulator-approved growth plan partly with Amazon and Alphabet data-center demand, priced for far less growth than it guides.
kill_criteria: The IURC gas-meter-accuracy investigation (hearing expected July 2026) results in a disallowance, penalty, or adverse safety finding
FY2026 non-GAAP consolidated adjusted EPS guidance ($2.02-$2.07) is cut at either of the next two quarterly releases
The guided 2026-2030 consolidated capital plan ($28.6 billion) is reduced by more than 10%
Either the Amazon or Alphabet data-center agreement referenced in the 2Q'26 release is terminated, reduced, or disclosed as impaired
Consolidated long-term debt rises to a level triggering a below-investment-grade downgrade at any major credit-rating agency
key_adverse_facts: IURC gas-meter accuracy investigation (opened Nov 2025): NIPSCO filed testimony in March 2026 and the hearing is now scheduled for October 2026 (Q2-26 10-Q), not July 2026 as the dossier assumed; separately in July 2026 the IURC opened formal investigations into authorised return on equity and the future use of regulatory trackers for Indiana electric utilities (omitted from the original dossier; DV30)

Q2-26 non-GAAP adjusted EPS fell to $0.16 from $0.22 (-27% YoY) and 1H-26 adjusted EPS is $1.22 vs $1.19 (+2.5%); the FY26 guide of $2.02-2.07 therefore depends on the seasonally strong second half (DV30)

Original claim that 1Q'26 GAAP net income was inflated by one-off Blackstone gains is not supported: 1Q'26 net income $507.1m vs $474.8m in 1Q'25 (seasonal gas-heating quarter) and 1H-26 non-GAAP adjustments are +$31.0m, i.e. adjusted net income ($587.2m) is above GAAP ($556.2m) (DV30)

Free cash flow is structurally negative in the current capex up-cycle (1H'26 capex $1,902.6m vs operating cash flow $1,122.7m); total debt $17.4bn at 30 Jun 2026 (long-term $15,612.6m + current $1,098.4m + short-term $692.0m) vs $16.2bn at 31 Dec 2025
data_conflicts: The Q15 triage's ~20% forward EPS growth conflicts with management's 9-10% non-GAAP EPS CAGR guide; the original dossier's explanation (one-off Blackstone gains in GAAP EPS) is not supported by the Q2-26 non-GAAP reconciliation (DV30), so the source of the 20% remains unexplained.
NI.confidence_in_thesis: med (guided capital plan and contracted data-center demand are well evidenced; open regulatory investigation and GAAP earnings-quality noise are unresolved as of this pass)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: DV30 (2026-10-08): the original 'P/E as perpetuity' reverse DCF (EPS treated as cash, 7.5% rate) implied 2.3%. On a dividend basis with programme inputs (D0 $1.20 = 4 x $0.30, price $39.25, cost of equity 7.65% = 5.17% + 0.60 x 4.14%, terminal growth 2.5-3.0%) the price needs 7.9-8.8%/yr dividend growth for ten years, against management's 9-10% EPS CAGR guide that the dossier adopts as its base: implied_vs_base is in_line (slightly below), not 'well below'. Verdict unchanged because INCLUDE-SMALL is consistent with in_line, but the 'priced for one-quarter of guided growth' rationale no longer holds.

NI.scenario_basis: Restated by DV30 for the dividend yield only: the original used ~1.5% but $1.20 / $39.25 = 3.1%. Same growth and exit-multiple assumptions (base 9-10% EPS growth, exit ~19.5x on FY26E $2.045; bear 3.5% growth, 16x; bull 13% growth, 21.5x); annualised 3-year total return including ~3.1% dividend yield.
